pairs.question: Heu, domine mi princeps, cui de te tantum licuit, cujus in te tanta surrexit audacia?
pairs.answer: Perdita est Antiochia, Franci tenent. Ego qualem vides terno lac vulnere vix aufugi.
pairs.derivation: The rustic, finding the wounded fugitive Cassianus, asks a real interrogative ("who dared so much against you, whose audacity rose against you?"); the framing "inquit" and the preceding narration of his amazement are dropped. Cassianus's reply answers it: the Franks hold Antioch and he barely escaped with three wounds. The window stops at "vix aufugi" (first full stop after the operative answer); what follows ("at tu, obsecro, ne palam facias... exspecta") turns from answering to a plea and bribe-offer, so it is cut; "inquit" framing inside the reply is dropped. "terno lac vulnere" kept verbatim as printed.

pairs.question: Quid sibi vult haec libratio?
pairs.answer: Imo, domine comes, alia est res, praesentia vestra non me sinit esse sollicitum, cui ludum struo dum trutino cultellum.
pairs.derivation: At dinner the count of Flanders asks Boamundus a genuine interrogative about his balancing of the knife. Only the interrogative is quoted as the question; his own following guess ("manifestum est, video, solliciti signum...") is his elaboration and is left out. Boamundus's answer refutes the anxiety-reading and gives the real reason (a game). The "inquit Boamundus" framing is dropped. The window ends at "trutino cultellum" (first full stop); the continuation "Hunc cujus grossitudo... in duo dispertiam" turns from answering to his boast about splitting the candle, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Hanccine beatorum turbam agnoscis, Anselle?
pairs.answer: Vix; neque enim alia ad cognoscendum signa remanserant, nisi qualibet quinquagenarium quempiam regressum agnoscimus, qui a nobis puer septenni est egressus.
pairs.derivation: Within Ansellus's reported dream a dead comrade asks a genuine interrogative ("Do you recognize this throng of the blessed?"); the "ille mihi sic ait" framing is dropped. Ansellus answers "Vix" and explains why recognition fails (the blessed appear aged beyond knowing); the "inquam" framing inside the reply is dropped. The window runs to the full stop at "est egressus"; the next sentence is the dead man's further speech ("Hi sunt Jerosolymipetae..."), not part of the answer.
